newsitem.title: CHINA: New China T-bond debuts with sharp price rise.
newsitem.headline: New China T-bond debuts with sharp price rise.

text.p: The price on China's latest three-year treasury bond rose 5.9 percent to 105.90 yuan in its debut on Tuesday from an issue price of 100.00 yuan in late afternoon trading.
The bond opened at 106.80 yuan and hit a high of 107.00 yuan in early trading before profit-taking pushed down the price.
The coupon for the new bond was 10.96 percent, the lowest for any three-year T-bond in China in the past four years.
Analysts said the bond was boosted by a bank interest rate cut by the People's Bank of China last week, the second cut his year.
"Despite its low coupon, falling bank interest rates have made the new bond still more profitable than bank deposits," said one analyst. "This attracted many investors today."
